title: The Rain and the Drying Racks

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — HONESTY AND ACCOUNTABILITY (HON-01 to HON-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Small lies, kind fibs, things left unsaid, things forgotten, honest mistakes and the odd careless one. Consequences stay the size of the mistake. Privacy is not lying, truth doesn't automatically fix things, and nobody has to confess, apologize or forgive.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager slept through the rain on their turn to bring in the drying fruit: rescue what you can, or wait for someone to ask.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: It was (subject)'s turn to bring in the drying fruit if it rained. Last night it rained. (subject) heard it start, thought, "It'll stop in a moment," and went back to sleep. It didn't stop. This morning the fruit on the racks is soggy, and some of it is already going soft.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) gets there before anyone else and spends the morning sorting: the firm pieces back out in the sun, the soft ones to be cooked today. When the others arrive, (subject.he/she) explains what happened. Some of the fruit is lost. "That's a lot of stewed fruit for tonight," (friend) observes. It is. It's good, too.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (subject) waits. Nobody asks. They just look at the racks, then up at the clouds, and then, one by one, at (subject). "I thought it would stop," (subject) says at last. "It didn't." They sort the fruit together. Nobody makes a fuss, which somehow makes (subject) feel worse, and more determined to get it right next time.
